brief.desc: Bearish, score 34. Gold is being sold through a real-yield tailwind: the oil shock has the market pricing a December Fed hike, and speculative positioning is still long enough to keep being liquidated. I hold this view with moderate confidence.
brief.yr: GLD closed $366.61 on October 23, down 0.65%, in a $364.33 to $369.25 range, and fell 4.03% on the week. Spot settled $3,994.01, down 0.74%, after an intraday low near $3,975, the weakest since July 20. The driver was oil: Houthi strikes inside Saudi Arabia lifted Brent to a five-month-plus high and CME FedWatch put December hike odds at 81%. The 10-year real yield rose only 2bp and DXY 0.20, so rates and the dollar did not cause the second straight down day.
brief.to: The base case (50%) is a hawkish FOMC hold on October 28 and firm PCE on October 29, keeping gold futures in a $3,850 to $4,050 range. The bear case (30%) is a break of the $3,890 52-week low toward $3,750 if Warsh validates a December hike or Brent tops $120. The bull case (20%) needs a Gulf de-escalation and real yields near 2.50%, for a squeeze to about $4,200. The week's key events are the FOMC on Wednesday and GDP plus PCE on Thursday at 8:30 ET. This view flips bullish if the 10-year TIPS real yield closes below 2.50% and December hike odds fall below 50% after the October 28 FOMC.

brief.why: The chain starts in the Gulf. Energy has held above $100 through the Iran conflict, and last week's Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and the US embassy evacuation turned an elevated oil price into a supply-risk premium. For a Fed with a hot inflation print behind it and jobless claims near 57-year lows at 194K, that keeps a December hike on the table; FedWatch has it at 81%. That is why the 2-year sat near 4.88% at the end of September and why the 10-year real yield climbed from 2.44% to 2.93% in September, a climb gold's slide followed almost tick for tick. What changed this week is that the link broke. On October 22 an equity scare over AI capex and tech credit sent money into Treasuries. Real yields fell 12bp and the 2-year 16bp, yet gold fell harder than on any day this month. In a risk-off move driven by a hawkish oil shock, gold is not the haven; it is a source of liquidity, because it is liquid, still carries gains from the run to $509.70 in GLD, and is held long by spec accounts. Breakevens falling 5bp the same day says bonds read oil as tightening, not reflating, which removes the inflation-hedge bid without the rate relief. Central banks, at about 63 tonnes in September on preliminary figures, are a floor, not an engine. Until the Fed path stops pricing hikes, price is set by the funds that need cash, and those funds are still long.
brief.cons: The loud story is oil to Fed hikes to gold down, with Goldman's $5,400 end-2027 target as the bulls' long-run anchor. The first half is right. The part being missed is positioning: after a 28% drawdown in GLD, Managed Money is still net long 104,206 contracts and long about 7.2 times its shorts (CFTC Disaggregated, October 20), and it trimmed only 3,777 longs in a week when price fell. That is not washed out. The crowded trade is the long, so the bearish call is not the crowded side, and the liquidation has room to run. Where consensus may be stretched: December hike odds of 80 to 90% already price a lot, so a hawkish hold that merely confirms them would not add new pressure. September ETF inflows were a record $10bn per the WGC, so the claim that ETF holders are dumping is not yet in the official data.
fals: Soften: a GLD close back above its 50-day average of $394.50, or gold futures above $4,150, in any session over the next two weeks would mean liquidation is done and move the score toward 45.
Invert: the 10-year Treasury real yield closing below 2.50% with December hike odds below 50% after the October 28 FOMC realigns rates and price bullishly; known by October 29 to 30.

Weak joint: the bear case assumes Western ETF holders are now selling, but the latest WGC data (September) showed record inflows and October flows were not checked; the WGC October report, due about the first week of November, or daily GLD holdings would test it.
